πίστεως δικαιουμένων· ἵν' οἱ μετὰ τὴν πίστιν ἐκεῖνοι γενόμενοι ἐκ περιτομῆς τοῦ
Ἀβραάμ, ἕτεροι ὄντες τῶν ἐκ πίστεως δικαιωθη σομένων τέκνων αὐτοῦ, ἢ εἰς τέκνα
αὐτοῦ λογισθησομένων, ἕτερος ὦσιν λαὸς παρὰ τὸν ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ ἐκ πίστεως
δικαιωθησόμενον· ἡ δὲ σφραγὶς ἐτηρεῖτο μὲν μὴ λυομένη, ὅσον οὐδέπω
ἐληλύθεισαν οἱ ἐκ πίστεως καὶ ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ· ἡνίκα δὲ ἦλθεν ὁ προειρημένος
τεχθήσεσθαι λαὸς τῶν ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ καὶ ἐκ πίστεως δικαιουμένων, τότε ἡ σφραγὶς
καὶ τὸ σημεῖον ἐκεῖνο ἐλύθη, ὥστ' ἂν λεχθῆναι τῷ βουλομένῳ τὴν σφραγῖδα
ἐκείνην λαβεῖν ὅτι ἐὰν περιτέμνη θε, Χρι τὸ ὑμᾶ οὐδὲν ὠφελή ει. 25 iv 15–17 ὁ γὰρ
νόμος ὀργὴν κατεργάζεται· οὗ γὰρ οὐκ ἔστι νόμος οὐδὲ παράβασις. διὰ τοῦτο ἐκ
πίστεως ἵνα κατὰ χάριν, εἰς τὸ εἶναι βεβαίαν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν παντὶ τῷ σπέρματι· οὐ
τῷ ἐκ τοῦ νόμου μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῷ ἐκ πίστεως Ἀβραάμ, ὅς ἐστι πατὴρ πάντων
ἡμῶν· καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν τέθεικά σε· κατέναντι οὗ
ἐπίστευσε θεοῦ τοῦ ζωοποιοῦντος τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ καλοῦντος τὰ μὴ ὄντα ὡς ὄντα.
ἀσυκοφαντήτως ἀκούειν χρὴ τοῦ ἀποστόλου ἐν τούτοις καὶ συνιέναι τοῦ
βουλήματος αὐτοῦ. φασὶ γάρ τινες· εἰ ἔνθα οὐκ ἔστι νόμος οὐδὲ παράβασις, δηλονότι
οὐδεὶς ἐν παραβάσει γέγονε πρὸ Μωσέως· εἰ δὲ μὴ γέγονέ τις, οὐδὲ ψεκτός· οὔτε οὖν
Κάιν οὔτε πάντες οἱ διὰ τὰς ἑαυτῶν ἁμαρτίας τὸν κατακλυ σμὸν παθόντες ἢ οἱ ἐν
Σοδόμοις ἐν παραβάσει γεγόνασιν· καὶ πρό γε τούτων Ἀδὰμ καὶ ἡ Εὖα. λεκτέον οὖν
πρὸς τούτους ὅτι ὁ Μωσέως νόμος οὐ τὴν ἐν τῇ κρίσει ὀργὴν κατεργάζεται ἀλλὰ τὴν
κατ' αὐτόν, τοὺς μὲν λιθολεύστους ποιῶν, ἑτέρους δὲ ἐπὶ πυρὸς κατακαίων, ἢ ἑτέρᾳ
ὑποβάλλων τιμωρίᾳ· ἀλλὰ καὶ εἴπερ οὗ οὐκ ἔστι νόμος οὐδὲ παράβασις, ὅτε ὅ α ὁ
νόμο λαλεῖ τοῖ ἐν τῷ νόμῳ λαλεῖ. ὅρα δὲ αὐτοὺς καὶ τὸν παρ' αὐτῷ Παύλῳ νόμον
πί τεω ὀνομαζό μενον θεοῦ ὀργὴν κατεργάζεσθαι, καὶ παράβασιν εἶναι ἔνθα ἐστὶν ὁ
τῆς πί στεως νόμος καὶ ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ, σαφῶς δὲ αὐτὸς ἕτερον μὲν εἶναι νόμον τὸν τοῦ
θεοῦ, ᾧ μόνῳ καὶ αὐτὸς υνήδεται κατὰ τὸν ἔ ω ἄνθρωπον, ἕτερον δὲ νόμον εἶναι
τὸν ἐν τοῖ μέλε ιν ἑαυτοῦ ἀντι τρατευόμενον τῷ νόμῳ τοῦ νοό . καὶ ὅρα μήποτε
οὗτος ἐστὶν ὁ ἀληθῶς ὀργὴν κατεργαζόμενος, καὶ οὗ οὐκ ἔστι νόμος οὗτος ἐκεῖ οὐδὲ
παράβασίς ἐστιν· καὶ οἱ ἐκ τούτου τοῦ νόμου οὐδαμῶς εἰσὶ κληρονόμοι, εἰ γὰρ οἱ ἐκ
νόμου κληρονόμοι κεκένωται ἡ πίστις. ἐν τῷ καταλόγῳ τῶν χαρισμάτων τῶν
διδομένων κατὰ τὴν ἀναλογίαν τῆ πί τεω , κατείλεκται καὶ ἡ πίστις· φησὶ γὰρ ὁ
Παῦλος μεθ' ἕτερα ἄλλῳ πί τι ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ πνεύματι. ὁ δ' αὐτός φησι καὶ ἀλλαχοῦ ὅτι
ἀπὸ θεοῦ ὑμῖν ἐχαρί θη οὐ μόνον τὸ εἰ Χρι τὸν πι τεύειν ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ
πά χειν. οἶμαι δὲ ὅτι καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι ἐλλιπῆ πεισθέντες εἶναι τὴν ἐκ τοῦ ἐφ' ἡμῖν
πίστιν ... εἰ καὶ ἐκ πίστεως οὖν οἱ κληρονόμοι καὶ ἡ ἐπαγγελία ἵνα κατὰ χάριν, οὐδ'
αὐτὴ ἡ πίστις ἡ πρὸ τῆς χάριτος, καθ' ἣν λέγεται διὰ τοῦτο ἐκ πίστεως ἵνα κατὰ
χάριν, χωρὶς χάριτος ὑφεστάναι οὐ δύναται. παντὶ δὲ τῷ σπέρματι, φησίν, ἤτοι τῷ ἐκ
τοῦ νόμου ἢ τῷ ἐκ τῆς πίστεως αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐ μόνον τῷ ἐκ τοῦ νόμου ἀλλ' εἰ ἔχοι
πρὸς τῷ ἐκ τοῦ νόμου τὸ ἐκ τῆς πίστεως. εἰ γὰρ μὴ οὕτως ἐκλάβοιμεν, ἔσται ἡ
ἐπαγγελία τοῖς ἐξ Ἰσμαὴλ καὶ τοῖς ἐκ Χεττούρας, ἅπερ οὐκ ἀρέσκει. (τοῦ αὐτοῦ)
ἀναγκαῖον δέ, φησίν, ἐξετάσαι φαίνεται πῶς ἀκολουθεῖ τῷ ἐκ πίστεως καὶ τῷ κατὰ
χάριν τὸ βεβαίαν εἶναι τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν· ἄρα γὰρ εἰ ἦν ἐκ νόμου, οὐχ οἷόν τε ἦν
βεβαίαν τυγχάνειν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν. πρόσχες οὖν οἱονεὶ δευσοποιός τις βαφὴ γίνεται
ἐκ πίστεως περὶ τὴν ψυχὴν καὶ μάλιστα τῆς λελογισμένης εἰς δικαιοσύνην, ὥστε τὴν
δι' αὐτῆς ἐπαγγελίαν καὶ χάριν ἴσχειν διὰ τὸ ἀνέκ πλυτον αὐτῆς, ἢ ἀμετάβολόν γε
τὴν βεβαιότητα· ἥτις οὐκ ἐμφαίνεται περὶ τὰ ἐκ νόμου ἔργα. ἀπο τρέφειν γοῦν ποτὲ
δίκαιο ἀπὸ τῆ δικαιο ύνη αὐτοῦ λέγεται καὶ ποιεῖν ἀδικίαν· οὐκ οἶδα δὲ εἰ καὶ περὶ
τῆς πίστεως γέγραπται ὅτι ἀπέστρεψέν τις ἀπὸ τῆς πίστεως, ἅπαξ μαρτυρηθεὶς
πεπιστευκέναι καὶ δικαιω θεὶς διὰ τὴν πίστιν. εἶτα καὶ τῇ μαρτυρίᾳ ἐπισφραγίζει ὁ
θεῖος ἀπόστολος τὸ εἰρημένον αὐτῷ. (τοῦ αὐτοῦ) [ὃ δὲ λέγει τοῦτό ἐστιν· ὥσπερ ὁ
θεὸς οὐκ ἔστι μερικὸς θεὸς ἀλλὰ πάντων πατήρ, οὕτω καὶ αὐτός. καὶ πάλιν ὥσπερ ὁ
θεὸς πατήρ ἐστιν οὐ κατὰ τὴν φυσικὴν συγγένειαν ἀλλὰ κατ' οἰκείωσιν πίστεως,
οὕτω καὶ αὐτός· ἡ γὰρ ὑπακοὴ ποιεῖ πατέρα πάντων ἡμῶν. ἐπειδὴ γὰρ οὐδὲν
pass_a_gloss: These, occurring and turning aside, in the manner of the sealed, the mystery of those justified by faith; so that those who, after that faith, became from the circumcision of Abraham, being others of those justified by faith, might be accounted as children of his, or be reckoned as his children, might be another people besides the one in uncircumcision justified by faith; but the seal was kept intact, as long as those from faith and in uncircumcision had not yet come; but when the previously mentioned people came to be formed from those in uncircumcision and justified by faith, then the seal and that sign were loosed, so that it might be said to the one desiring to take that seal that if he circumcises, Christ will profit him nothing. 25 iv 15–17 For the law works wrath; for where there is no law, neither is there transgression. Therefore it is of faith, that it might be according to grace, to the end that the promise might be sure to all the seed; not only to that which is of the law, but also to that which is of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all, as it is written, 'I have made you a father of many nations'; before whom he believed God, who quickens the dead, and calls those things which are not as though they were. One must hear the apostle in these things without contention and understand his purpose. For some say, 'If in that place there is no law nor transgression, then undoubtedly no one has been in transgression before Moses'; but if no one has been in transgression, then no one is worthy of blame; neither Cain nor all those who, on account of their own sins, suffered the flood, nor those who were in transgression in Sodom; and even before these, Adam and Eve. It must be said to them that the law of Moses does not work the wrath in judgment, but works wrath according to itself, making some stone-cutters, others burning in fire, or subjecting others to another punishment; but even if where there is no law nor transgression, the law speaks to those in the law. Look also at them and at the law beside Paul, called the law of faith, working God's wrath, and transgression being where the law of faith and the law of God are; but clearly he is another law, namely the law of God, by which alone he delights according to the inward man; but another law, namely the law in the members of himself, warring against the law of the mind. And see lest this be the one truly working wrath, and where there is no law, this is neither transgression; and those who are of this law are in no way heirs, for if those who are of the law are heirs, faith is made void. In the catalogue of the charismata given according to the proportion of faith, faith is also enumerated; for Paul says, with other things, to another faith in the same Spirit. And the same says elsewhere that from God he has graciously granted you not only that you might attain Christ, but also that you might suffer for his sake. But I think that the apostles, being weakly persuaded, are to be in the faith which is in us... even if therefore the heirs and the promise are that it might be according to grace, yet this faith which is before grace, by which it is said that it is of faith that it might be according to grace, cannot subsist without grace. And to all the seed, he says, either to that which is of the law or to that which is of the faith of Abraham, and not only to that which is of the law but also if he should have that which is of the faith besides that which is of the law. For if we do not thus obtain, the promise will be to those from Ishmael and those from Keturah, which is not pleasing. (of the same) It is necessary, he says, it appears to examine how the being according to faith and according to grace follows the promise being sure; for if it were of the law, it would not be possible to obtain the sure promise. Therefore consider, as if a dyer were dyeing, that the dyeing is made by faith concerning the soul, and especially the reasoning accounted to righteousness, so that the promise and grace through it might have, by its inexhaustibleness, or by its immutability, the certainty; which does not appear concerning the works of the law. Sometimes he feeds the righteous from his own righteousness and does evil; but I do not know whether it is written concerning faith that anyone has turned away from faith, having once been testified to have believed and been justified by faith. Then also the divine apostle seals with his testimony the thing said to him. (of the same) [But what he says this is: as God is not a partial God but the Father of all, so also he; and again, as God is Father not according to natural kinship but according to the familiarity of faith, so also he; for obedience makes a father of all of us. Since neither]
pass_b_english: When the faithful turn aside like the sealed, the mystery of those justified by faith unfolds. Those who, after believing, emerge from Abraham’s circumcision—yet remain distinct from the faithful—may be counted as his children or reckoned as his offspring, forming a people apart from the uncircumcised justified by faith. The seal remained intact as long as no one from faith and uncircumcision had arrived. But when the foretold people formed from the uncircumcised justified by faith appeared, the seal and its sign were loosed, so that it could be said to the one desiring that seal: if you circumcise, Christ profits you nothing. For the law brings wrath; where there is no law, there is no transgression. Therefore, the promise comes through faith, so that it may rest upon grace, ensuring the promise is sure for all Abraham’s seed—not only those under the law, but also those who share Abraham’s faith, who is father of us all, as it is written: ‘I have made you a father of many nations.’ Before him, he believed in God, who gives life to the dead and calls into being what does not exist. One must hear the apostle here without contention and grasp his intent. Some claim: ‘If there is no law nor transgression in that place, then surely no one transgressed before Moses.’ But if no one transgressed, then no one is blameworthy—not Cain, nor those who perished in the flood due to their own sins, nor the Sodomites in transgression, nor even Adam and Eve. Yet it must be told them: the Mosaic law does not work wrath in judgment, but wrath according to itself—making some stonecutters, others burning in fire, or subjecting others to another punishment. Even where there is no law nor transgression, the law still speaks to those under the law. Observe them and the law beside Paul, called the law of faith, which works God’s wrath, and where transgression occurs when the law of faith and the law of God intersect. But clearly, he is another law—namely, the law of God, by which alone he delights in the inward man. Yet another law exists: the law in his members, warring against the law of the mind. Beware lest this be the true worker of wrath; and where there is no law, this is neither transgression. Those under this law are in no way heirs, for if those under the law are heirs, faith is rendered void. In the catalogue of charismata distributed according to the measure of faith, faith itself is enumerated—for Paul says, with other gifts, to another faith in the same Spirit. And elsewhere he declares that from God he has graciously granted you not only to attain Christ, but also to suffer for his sake. But I think the apostles, being weakly persuaded, are to be in the faith that dwells in us… Even if the heirs and the promise are to be according to grace, yet this faith which precedes grace—by which it is said that it is of faith that it might be according to grace—cannot subsist without grace. And to all the seed, he says: either to those of the law or to those of Abraham’s faith, and not only to those of the law, but also if one should possess Abraham’s faith in addition to the law. For if we do not thus obtain, the promise will fall to those from Ishmael and those from Keturah, which is not pleasing. (Of the same) It is necessary, he says, it appears, to examine how being according to faith and according to grace follows the promise being sure; for if it were of the law, obtaining the sure promise would be impossible. Therefore, consider, as if a dyer were dyeing: the dyeing is made by faith concerning the soul, and especially the reasoning accounted to righteousness, so that the promise and grace through it might possess, by its inexhaustibility or immutability, certainty—which does not appear concerning the works of the law. Sometimes he feeds the righteous from his own righteousness and does evil; but I do not know whether it is written concerning faith that anyone has turned away from faith, having once been testified to have believed and been justified by faith. Then also the divine apostle seals with his testimony the thing said to him. (Of the same) [But what he says this is: as God is not a partial God but the Father of all, so also he; and again, as God is Father not according to natural kinship but according to the familiarity of faith, so also he; for obedience makes a father of all of us. Since neither]

bible_refs.note: Pass A references Romans 4:16 regarding the promise being sure to all seed through faith.
Pass A quotes Genesis 17:5: ‘I have made you a father of many nations’ in reference to Abraham.
Reference to Abraham's circumcision as a seal and the faith of the uncircumcised.
Discussion of law, faith, grace, and the promise to Abraham's seed.
Abraham's faith in God who gives life to the dead and calls things not existing as existing.
Faith excludes boasting; law upheld through faith, not nullified.
